records.title: Launch route families still mount fail-open, and neither boot nor /readyz checks that launch prefixes are mounted
records.evidenceAtHead: (1) `grep -rn "Failed to mount" server/bootstrap/*.ts | wc -l` = 172 at HEAD (173 at 92ccdba1). These are log-and-continue catch blocks, and launch prefixes sit inside them: /api/projects (server/bootstrap/register-project-routes.ts:31-36), /api/authoring (register-inline-routes.ts:317-323), /api/ectd (register-document-routes.ts:123-144), /api/c2c/project-vault (register-clinical-intel-routes.ts:186-193). A heuristic scan of the 129 apiPrefixes claimed by LAUNCH_SURFACE_IDS surfaces found at least 40 mounted inside try/catch. (2) mountAll still logs and skips a router with no default export (server/bootstrap/mount-routes.ts:77-80). (3) /readyz (server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts:50-180) checks database, schema, ana, storage, redis and worker. It has no route or mount check. `git diff 92ccdba1 HEAD -- server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts` touches only the shadow-health handler, and server/startup/routes.ts and server/bootstrap/mount-routes.ts are unchanged since the audit. (4) No mount registry and no router-stack walk exist anywhere in server/: a grep for router.stack, LAUNCH_APPS or assertLaunch hits only server/mcp/auth/connector-enablement.ts. (5) .env.example:808 still has STRICT_STARTUP_INVARIANTS=false, no terraform or workflow sets it, and the invariants it gates (server/index.ts:187-210) include no route check anyway. (6) The CI 'Production Image Boot' job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:2102-2236) requires /healthz and /readyz to return 200 and signs a user in (scripts/ci/image-boot-signin.mjs, auth endpoints only). It probes no launch route. server/bootstrap/__tests__/registered-routers-load.test.ts covers only static `from '../routes/x.js'` imports, not the `await import()` try/catch blocks.
records.remaining: Everything in the finding. When a launch router throws at import or module-evaluation time, the error becomes a console.error. Unmatched /api paths then fall to the JSON 404 catch-all (server/startup/services.ts:582) while /readyz returns 200 and the deploy is green. No production boot assertion derives the required prefixes from LAUNCH_APPS, and /readyz reports nothing about missing launch routes.
records.severityRationale: Production modules refuse at import time when configuration is missing, which the terraform comments describe as 'import-time refusals'. One such refusal, or a missing asset, inside a launch router silently 404s a launch app for the pilot tenant while health and readiness stay green. The validated state ('all launch functions present') then cannot be demonstrated from the running system. This is an integrity and operability gap rather than an active exposure, so it is not P0.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this while every router loads. If a router fails to import, a launch screen (Projects, Vault, Authoring, eCTD compile) shows a load error or JSON 404 while /readyz still says ready. Workaround: before each test session, grep the server boot log for 'Failed to mount' and restart or fix before testing.
records.instructions:
1. Create server/bootstrap/mount-registry.ts. It exports instrumentAppUse(app: Express), which wraps app.use exactly once: when the first argument is a string or an array of strings, it records each path in a module-level Set and then delegates to the original. It also exports mountedPrefixes(): ReadonlySet<string>. Call instrumentAppUse(app) in server/index.ts immediately after `const app = express()` (line 93), before mountFastPathHealthEndpoints (line 113), so it covers both registerPreStartRoutes and registerPostStartRoutes and every mountAll call.
2. Create server/startup/launch-mount-assertion.ts. requiredLaunchPrefixes() returns the union of UI_SURFACES[].apiPrefixes (shared/constants/ui-surface-registry.ts:155) for every surface id in LAUNCH_SURFACE_IDS (shared/constants/launch-scope.ts:206), minus NEVER_GATED (server/services/entitlements/api-prefix-map.ts:23), minus an explicit LAUNCH_MOUNT_EXCEPTIONS map of prefix to written reason (an entry without a reason fails). missingLaunchPrefixes(mounted) returns every required prefix P for which no mounted M satisfies M === P, P.startsWith(M + '/') or M.startsWith(P + '/').
3. Create server/startup/route-readiness-state.ts, modelled on readiness-state.ts, with state 'unknown' | 'ok' | 'missing' and a detail list of missing prefixes. In server/index.ts, right after `await registerPostStartRoutes(routeCtx)` (line 227) and before mountApiCatchAll(app), compute missing and record the state. When NODE_ENV === 'production' and missing is non-empty, log every missing prefix and process.exit(1). Provide no environment bypass in production.
4. In server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts /readyz (lines 50-180), add deps.routes, which fails closed on 'unknown' and 'missing'. Put routesDetail (the missing prefixes) in the 503 body, and report the route state on the 200 body too, as the schema and AnA verdicts already are.
5. Make the launch-app mounts in log-and-continue blocks fail loudly in production. At minimum: register-project-routes.ts:31-36, register-inline-routes.ts:317-323, register-document-routes.ts:123-144 and register-clinical-intel-routes.ts:186-193. Either convert them to static imports through mountAll, or rethrow inside the catch when NODE_ENV === 'production'. Step 3 is the backstop for the remaining 172 catches.
6. Tests (make each fail first). Add server/startup/__tests__/launch-mount-assertion.test.ts. (a) Instrument a fresh express app and mount every required prefix except /api/c2c/project-vault. Expect exactly that prefix missing. Before step 2 exists, stub missingLaunchPrefixes to return [] and show the test red. (b) vi.mock('../../routes/c2c/project-vault', () => { throw new Error('boom') }), run registerClinicalIntelRoutes on an instrumented app, and expect the prefix missing. Add a /readyz test that sets the route state to 'missing' and expects 503 with failed containing 'routes'.
7. In .github/workflows/ci.yml 'Production Image Boot' (lines 2160-2218), after /readyz=200, assert that the /readyz body has dependencies.routes === 'ok'. Show it red once by running that job's script against an image whose project-vault import is made to throw.
8. Commit on concept2cure-v2 and push (Rule 0). Never rebase.
records.acceptance: (a) The new unit test is shown red before the assertion exists or with it stubbed, and green after. (b) In production mode (NODE_ENV=production), forcing the project-vault import to throw makes boot exit non-zero with '/api/c2c/project-vault' named in the log. (c) With the state forced to 'missing', /readyz returns 503 with failed including 'routes' and routesDetail listing the prefixes. (d) The CI Production Image Boot job asserts dependencies.routes === 'ok' on the real image and fails when a launch router is broken. (e) An entry in LAUNCH_MOUNT_EXCEPTIONS without a reason fails the test.
records.dependencies: None. Complements ARCH-01 (production mount manifest equals the launch catalog) and ARCH-09 (path normalization in the scope gate).

records.title: The four named security and migration gates now run blocking in CI. Two newer migration gates (guard-order, manifest sync) are hook-only again, and nothing prevents recurrence
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED PART: .github/workflows/ci.yml:575-598 is the step 'Security gates that ran only in the pre-push hook', in the lint job, with no continue-on-error. It runs ci:unauthenticated-fetch, ci:drizzle-tenant-scope, ci:migration-drop-safety and ci:upload-guards, each after its :selftest. At 92ccdba1, ci.yml had 0 matches for these four. ci.yml triggers on push to every branch (lines 3-11). tests/ci/ci-honesty.contract.test.ts:87-123 pins each gate as invoked on a trunk push and checks that its failure fails the step (runWithFailingGate). In .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:84-150, the ci-verdict job refuses to deploy a SHA that lacks a successful push run of ci.yml, semgrep.yml and codeql.yml on concept2cure-v2, so CI is a hard deploy gate (required status checks are moot on a push-only trunk). REMAINING: I compared every `npm run` in .husky/pre-push with .github/workflows/*.yml. These are still hook-only: ci:migration-guard-order and its :selftest (.husky/pre-push:148; this gate keeps the qms_documents Part 11 signature triggers from being ordered before the CREATE, and was added in dc0fb95b4 on 2026-10-12, after the audit), db:sync-manifest:check (:272), ci:undefined-css-classes (:305) and ci:class-vocabulary (:186). The diff-scoped ci:pushed-lint-errors, ci:pushed-lint-warnings and ci:pushed-typecheck have full-tree CI equivalents. The ci-honesty GATES list is hand-maintained, so new hook gates are not caught. In this clone `git config core.hooksPath` is unset and .git/hooks holds only *.sample, so the hook runs nowhere here. I ran the hook-only migration gates at HEAD: check-migration-guard-order.mjs printed OK, its --selftest printed OK, and sync-migration-manifest.mjs --check printed 'Manifest is in sync'. There is no live defect; they are simply unenforced.
records.remaining: ci:migration-guard-order (+selftest) and db:sync-manifest:check (migration safety), plus ci:undefined-css-classes and ci:class-vocabulary (UI hygiene), run only in .husky/pre-push. No CI parity check makes a new pre-push gate also run in CI. The ci-honesty contract's GATES list is hand-maintained.
records.severityRationale: The security-critical gates named in the finding (tenant scope, drop safety, unauthenticated fetch, upload guards) are closed and deploy-gated. The remaining migration gates pass at HEAD. The residual risk is a future misordered QMS migration pushed from a clone without the hook. It would deploy green and open a window in which qms_documents can reach 'effective' without a Part 11 signature. That is a regression guard, not a live defect.
records.instructions:
1. In .github/workflows/ci.yml, step 'Security gates that ran only in the pre-push hook' (lines 575-598), append `npm run ci:migration-guard-order:selftest`, `npm run ci:migration-guard-order` and `npm run db:sync-manifest:check`. Update the step comment.
2. Add a lint-job step that runs `npm run ci:undefined-css-classes` and `npm run ci:class-vocabulary`. Both are textual and cheap. Use `if: "!cancelled() && steps.install.conclusion == 'success'"` and no continue-on-error.
3. In tests/ci/ci-honesty.contract.test.ts, add 'ci:migration-guard-order:selftest', 'ci:migration-guard-order' and 'db:sync-manifest:check' to GATES (lines 91-105).
4. Add scripts/ci/check-hook-ci-parity.mjs and package.json scripts 'ci:hook-ci-parity' and 'ci:hook-ci-parity:selftest'. The script parses every `npm run [--silent] <name>` in .husky/pre-push and resolves each name through package.json scripts. Each one passes only if some .github/workflows/*.yml `run:` that executes on push to concept2cure-v2 invokes the npm name or the script file it maps to. Otherwise it must be listed in a new scripts/ci/hook-only-gates.json with a non-empty reason. Seed that file with ci:pushed-lint-errors, ci:pushed-lint-warnings and ci:pushed-typecheck (diff-scoped variants of CI's full lint/typecheck), ci:server-error-leaks:write-baseline and db:sync-manifest (writers, not gates), and ci:untracked-imports (pushed-diff scoped; CI runs its selftest at ci.yml:377-379). An entry without a reason fails. The --selftest copies the hook to a temp file with an injected `npm run --silent ci:fake-gate`, and it must fail. It must also fail on an allowlist entry with an empty reason.
5. Run `npm run ci:hook-ci-parity:selftest && npm run ci:hook-ci-parity` in the lint job, and add both names to the ci-honesty GATES.
6. Verify by making each gate fail first. Locally, move 20260511_qms_and_labeling.sql after 20261001_qms_document_signature_required.sql in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES, run the new CI step through tests/ci/workflow-harness.ts (the ci-honesty test does this via runWithFailingGate), confirm red, and revert. Before step 1, show ci:hook-ci-parity failing on the current tree, then green after.
7. Commit on concept2cure-v2 and push (Rule 0).
records.acceptance: (a) ci-honesty.contract.test.ts includes the three migration gates and passes; with any one of them removed from ci.yml, it fails. (b) ci:hook-ci-parity is red on the tree before step 1 (it lists migration-guard-order, sync-manifest:check, undefined-css-classes and class-vocabulary) and green after. Its selftest fails on an injected hook gate and on an allowlist entry without a reason. (c) A push whose migration set orders the QMS creator after its Part 11 trigger file turns ci.yml red, so deploy-aws.yml ci-verdict refuses the deploy.

records.title: AnA's DOCX tools now ship with a pinned Python runtime, and run_python_script runs only in a hardened container. Residuals: no runtime probe, unavailable tools still offered to the model, a dead ingestion fallback
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED (the core impact): Dockerfile.optimized:76 installs python3-venv. Lines 89-94 build the /opt/docx-runtime virtualenv with python-docx and lxml at the requirements.txt pins (requirements.txt:19-20), plus a build-time import probe. Line 95 sets ENV ANA_DOCX_PYTHON, and line 172 copies workers/artifact-compute. None of these lines existed at 92ccdba1. Both spawners use ANA_DOCX_PYTHON (server/services/compute/scriptWorker.ts:65, workerClient.ts:51). I ran scripts/ci/check-image-document-runtime.mjs: 'OK — 4 runtime(s) copied, their imports installed and probed'. Its node test, scripts/ci/__tests__/image-document-runtime.test.mjs, passes 8/8 and runs in CI via `npm run test:ci-scripts` (ci.yml:1124-1126). The CI Production Image Boot job builds the image (ci.yml:2102), so the import probe executes. workers/artifact-compute/python-script-runtime.py, the in-process socket-monkeypatch sandbox, was deleted in 930fe7b4c. The run_python_script handler (server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts:7711-7771) now runs model code only through containerExec.runInContainer: `docker run --network none --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --read-only --user 1000:1000` with pids, memory and CPU limits (server/services/compute/containerExec.ts:68-98). It returns available:false and runs nothing when ANA_ENABLE_CONTAINER_EXEC !== 'true' (lines 7730-7739). The remaining runtimes contain no exec, eval, compile, subprocess or socket (grep). insert_clause_template uses the docx-insert runtime (server/services/ana/clause-templates.ts:8). RESIDUAL: (a) Nothing probes the runtimes at boot or in /readyz; the only probe is the build-time import. (b) run_python_script and run_in_container stay in the tool list given to the model (getAllEnabledTools, server/services/ana/AnaToolDefinitions.ts ~2888) even where container exec is disabled or Docker is absent, as on ECS Fargate, and .env.example:616 defaults ANA_ENABLE_CONTAINER_EXEC=true. (c) server/services/unifiedDocumentIngestion.js:91-140 still falls back to .venv/bin/python3 plus ingestion/pdf_extractor.py, which the image does not ship, and spawns it with the full process.env. It is reachable only via /api/knowledge-base (server/routes/knowledge-base.ts:1671), which no client/src file calls. (d) server/requirements.txt still says `-r ../services/requirements.txt`, and that file does not exist.
records.remaining: (a) No boot or /readyz probe that runs each runtime. (b) run_python_script and run_in_container are offered to the model where they cannot run, and .env.example defaults container exec to true. (c) The dead Python PDF fallback in unifiedDocumentIngestion.js, which also leaks the full env to its child. (d) The broken server/requirements.txt include. Whether model-written code execution is in the launch scope at all is still a founder decision (arch report open question 2).
records.severityRationale: The finding's impact is closed. The production image (AWS and compose) now ships and build-probes the document runtimes, and model-written code no longer runs in the API process. The residuals are honest failures (an explicit 'not available' result or a worker error), not fabricated output or exposure, so they are polish.
records.humanTestingNote: Images built from Dockerfile.optimized (docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.beta.yml, AWS) have working DOCX tools. On a bare `npm run dev` without python-docx and lxml installed, insert_document_content, surgical_docx_xml_edit, validate_docx and insert_clause_template fail with a worker error ('ModuleNotFoundError: docx'). run_python_script says it is not available unless Docker is reachable and ANA_ENABLE_CONTAINER_EXEC=true. Workaround: `python3 -m venv .docx && .docx/bin/pip install python-docx==1.2.0 lxml==6.1.1`, then set ANA_DOCX_PYTHON=$PWD/.docx/bin/python, or test against the compose-built image.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decision first: are run_python_script and run_in_container in the launch scope? If not, go to step 3. If yes, fund an isolated execution service; ECS Fargate has no Docker daemon, so container exec cannot work in the API task.
2. Add server/startup/document-runtime-probe.ts, called from server/startup/services.ts at boot. It spawns `${ANA_DOCX_PYTHON || 'python3'} workers/artifact-compute/docx-validate-runtime.py` on a minimal fixture .docx (checked in under workers/artifact-compute/fixtures/) through the existing runPythonRuntime path in server/services/compute/scriptWorker.ts, and records 'ok' | 'down' | 'unknown' in a readiness-state module. Add deps.documentRuntime to /readyz in server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts (lines 50-180). In production it fails closed on 'unknown' and 'down'. Test: with ANA_DOCX_PYTHON=/bin/false the probe reports 'down' and /readyz returns 503. Show this red before the probe exists.
3. In server/services/ana/AnaToolDefinitions.ts getAllEnabledTools() (~line 2888), filter out run_python_script and run_in_container when getContainerExecConfig().enabled is false (server/services/compute/containerExec.ts:44). Keep the handler refusals (AnaToolExecutor.ts:7730-7739 and ~8156-8165) as the backstop. Change .env.example:616 to ANA_ENABLE_CONTAINER_EXEC=false and note that ECS Fargate has no Docker. Unit test: with the flag unset, neither tool is in getAllEnabledTools(); with it set, both are.
4. In server/services/unifiedDocumentIngestion.js:91-140, replace the direct-spawn fallback with an explicit `{ success: false, strategy: 'none', warnings: ['PDF text extraction service is not available in this deployment'] }` and spawn nothing. This also removes the `...process.env` pass-through. This is a server-internal fallback with no client caller (no /api/knowledge-base call in client/src), so no user-facing capability is deleted; name the Vault's canonical PDF text extraction path in the commit message.
5. Fix server/requirements.txt: point it at `-r ../requirements.txt`, or delete it after `git grep -n 'server/requirements.txt'` shows no reader.
6. Commit on concept2cure-v2 and push (Rule 0).
records.acceptance: (a) The /readyz test is red with ANA_DOCX_PYTHON=/bin/false and green with the image virtualenv, and the CI Production Image Boot job sees dependencies.documentRuntime === 'ok'. (b) With ANA_ENABLE_CONTAINER_EXEC unset, getAllEnabledTools() contains neither run_python_script nor run_in_container (a unit test, shown failing first). (c) unifiedDocumentIngestion.js no longer references .venv/bin/python3 or ingestion/pdf_extractor.py. (d) `pip install -r server/requirements.txt --dry-run` resolves, or the file is gone.
records.dependencies: Founder decision on whether model-written code execution (run_python_script, run_in_container) is in the launch scope (arch report open question 2). ARCH-03 (AnA production allowlist) would subsume step 3.

records.title: The tenant directory (/api/tenants GET, POST, PATCH and /:tenantId/users) still runs on a separate porsager client as the DB owner role, outside RLS and the canonical pool
records.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:6 still has `import postgres from 'postgres'`, and lines 66-75 still build `const sql = postgres(cleanDatabaseUrl(process.env.DATABASE_URL || process.env.DATABASE_NEON_NEW_SECRET))`. Four handlers query through it: GET / (lines 129-145), POST / INSERT INTO organizations (177-193), PATCH /:id UPDATE organizations (262-277) and GET /:tenantId/users (324-341). Only DELETE, cancel-deletion and purge use the canonical pool (lines 411, 452, 510), and that was already true at 92ccdba1. `git diff 92ccdba1 HEAD` on the file changes only authorization comments and helpers. The canonical pool connects as APP_DATABASE_URL (app_service, NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS), with RLS startup options and the boot assertion assertRlsEnforcementForProduction (server/db/runtime.ts:41-67). DATABASE_URL in production is the owner role c2c_admin. terraform/stack/main.tf:43-47 says so itself: tenants-simple 'serves routes through a client on it, outside RLS. A known exposure'. Both URLs are injected into the API task (main.tf:316-317). server/middleware/establishRequestTenantScope.ts:88-96 likewise says 'The bypass connection remains an RLS-governance gap'. The router is mounted at /api/tenants (server/bootstrap/register-tenant-routes.ts:51), and client/src/contexts/TenantContext.tsx:152 calls it on every shell load. Application-layer checks are present: resolvePlatformAdmin with no org-admin bypass, the membership join (line 128) and the authedOrgId check (line 319). Other secondary drivers are still in package.json dependencies: postgres ^3.4.9 (also used by scripts/verify-migration.mjs and tests/migrations/proofAuditLogs.test.ts), @neondatabase/serverless ^1.1.0 (server/scripts/direct_import.js, scripts/fix-missing-schema.cjs) and @supabase/supabase-js ^2.110.0. server/services/indCopilot.js:11-21 builds a service-role client when SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are set, and is reachable via server/routes/ind.ts:17. No lint or CI rule forbids new pools or drivers outside server/db: scripts/ci/check-legacy-dep-quarantine.mjs quarantines only supabase and aws-sdk v2.
records.remaining: Everything in the finding. Four request handlers on a launch-shell path run as the RLS-exempt owner role on a second driver, outside the boot RLS posture probe and the pool instrumentation. postgres, @neondatabase/serverless and @supabase/supabase-js are still runtime dependencies. No gate forbids new pools.
records.severityRationale: Tenant-isolation defense in depth. The tenant directory, including user emails and roles, is served through the owner (DDL-capable, RLS-exempt) credential, which contradicts the 'runtime connects as NOBYPASSRLS' control a GxP security review will be shown. The terraform labels it a known exposure. The application-layer checks are currently correct, so this is not an active cross-tenant leak (not P0), but it should close before pilot users rely on production. Effort is S.
records.instructions:
1. In server/routes/tenants-simple.ts, delete the porsager client: the import at line 6, cleanDatabaseUrl (lines 44-63) and lines 66-75. Run every query through the request-scoped client the auth boundary provides, `const db = req.dbClient ?? pool` (pool is already imported at line 14 from '../db'), as parameterized `db.query(text, values)`.
2. Convert the four handlers. GET / (lines 128-145): two parameterized SELECTs. POST / (177-193): INSERT ... RETURNING with $1..$9. PATCH /:id (262-277): `SET name = COALESCE($1, name), slug = COALESCE($2, slug), ...` in place of the nested sql`name` fragments. GET /:tenantId/users (324-341). Keep the 23505 / organizations_slug_unique mapping; pg errors carry .code and .constraint the same way.
3. Scope. '/api/tenants' is in SYSTEM_SCOPE_PREFIXES (server/middleware/establishRequestTenantScope.ts:77-98), so every request currently runs under the system scope. Run the non-platform-admin branches (the member branch of GET /, and GET /:tenantId/users when authedOrgId(req) === tenantId) under the caller's tenant scope via runWithTenantScope (server/db/tenantStore.ts:74), or narrow the system scope to the requirePlatformAdmin routes, so RLS filters as defense in depth. Keep resolvePlatformAdmin and the authedOrgId check unchanged.
4. Update the comments that describe the exposure: terraform/stack/main.tf:43-47 (DATABASE_URL no longer serves routes) and establishRequestTenantScope.ts:88-96.
5. Remove the extra drivers. Port scripts/verify-migration.mjs and tests/migrations/proofAuditLogs.test.ts to pg, then drop 'postgres' from package.json. Port or delete server/scripts/direct_import.js and scripts/fix-missing-schema.cjs (offline scripts, not user-facing), then drop '@neondatabase/serverless'. In server/services/indCopilot.js:11-21, replace the Supabase reads with pool queries (or remove the branch, which is null unless SUPABASE_* is set), move scripts/setup_reference_model.js to pg, drop '@supabase/supabase-js', and shrink SUPABASE_ALLOWLIST in scripts/ci/check-legacy-dep-quarantine.mjs:23-26 to empty.
6. Add a gate: extend scripts/ci/check-legacy-dep-quarantine.mjs (already run at .github/workflows/ci.yml:863), or add ci:single-db-pool with a :selftest. It refuses, outside server/db/** and test files, any import of 'postgres', '@neondatabase/serverless' or '@supabase/supabase-js', and any `new Pool(` / `new pg.Pool(`. Baseline existing script violators (e.g. server/scripts/run-sql.js:30) with a written reason. The selftest writes a temp server/routes/__fixture__.ts that imports 'postgres' and must fail.
7. Tests (make each fail first). Extend server/__tests__/security/tenant-isolation-tenants-simple.contract.test.ts to assert that tenants-simple.ts does not import 'postgres' and that every query goes through req.dbClient or pool; it is red at HEAD. Add tests/db/tenants-directory-rls.dbtest.ts on the app_service role: a member's GET /api/tenants returns only their organisations, and GET /api/tenants/:otherOrg/users returns 403.
8. Commit on concept2cure-v2 and push (Rule 0).
records.acceptance: (a) The contract test is red at HEAD and green after. (b) `git grep -nE "from 'postgres'|@neondatabase/serverless|@supabase/supabase-js" -- server shared` returns nothing, and package.json no longer lists the three packages. (c) The new pool or driver gate's selftest fails on an injected fixture, and the gate passes on the tree. (d) The db test shows the member-scoped directory under app_service, and a platform admin still sees all organisations. (e) The terraform comment no longer lists tenants-simple as an exposure.
